//Skydio

📍San Mateo, CA

Tech: Autonomous flight

Platform: Fixed-wing aircraft

Goal: Give responders a live aerial view over long distances, where quadcopters cannot reach.

Why: Rural emergencies can wait 45 minutes or more for a deputy, and utility fault searches along transmission lines are slow.

Traction: Deploying to customers in 2027, per Skydio.

Skydio's F10 Lightrunner is a fixed-wing aircraft built for emergency response, search and rescue, and asset inspection missions measured in miles. It is designed to launch and catch itself through a suction-based robotic gripper, fly at speeds up to 100 mph, and be housed in a MegaDock that holds up to five F10s. Skydio says a single MegaDock, with F10's 30-mile flight radius, gives one launch location a reach of nearly 3,000 square miles, which the company says could bring a 15-minute response to a rural county.

The aircraft uses the same autonomy engine as Skydio's X10 quadcopter, extended to a form factor built for distance and speed. Skydio says Pathfinder plans the route before launch, and Foresight adjusts the flight path in real time to keep the subject in view.

Skydio says F10 deploys to customers in 2027 and that customers can talk to sales now to get in line. Skydio also announced the Asset Command and Security Command software platforms, which are available to purchase now with general availability early next year.

Source: Skydio, Inc., September 24, 2026

fields.headline: STATE WIDENS ID CHECKS
fields.deck: The award is up to $6.5 million through 2031.

stories.caption:
The U.S. State Department awarded facial recognition developer Paravision a contract worth up to $6.5 million on September 23, for what federal procurement records describe as "digital detection/identity assurance." The firm-fixed-price contract runs through September 22, 2031, and the department initially obligated $1.3 million.

The State Department competed the award under simplified acquisition procedures as a total small-business set-aside, and it received a single offer. Public award records do not identify which Paravision products were purchased. The description overlaps with Paravision's deepfake detection and liveness detection technology, which the company markets to protect digital identity systems against manipulated and AI-generated faces, but the record does not confirm that either product is included.

The September contract is much larger than an earlier April 30 State Department purchase from Paravision, a $24,717 purchase card order for a software license. Public records do not show whether that purchase was a test, pilot or precursor to the larger award.

Source: Biometric Update, October 17, 2026

Image: Biometric Update (courtesy)

//Seasats

📍San Diego, CA

Tech: Autonomous surveillance

Platform: Unmanned surface vessel

Goal: Detect illegal maritime activity, including drug trafficking and unauthorized vessel ingress, in the Gulf of America.

Why: Crewed patrols are limited by crew endurance, operating cost and the area one asset can cover at a time.

Private company → Backers: Shield Capital, L3Harris Technologies, Konvoy Ventures

Traction: Lightfish vessels deployed in the Gulf of America for U.S. maritime border security, expanding Operation River Wall work on the Rio Grande since January 2026, per Seasats.

Seasats said on Oct. 2, 2026 that it has deployed a fleet of Lightfish unmanned surface vessels for U.S. maritime border security. The vessels launched from the Texas coast and will run persistent autonomous surveillance, building on the company's earlier support of Operation River Wall.

Each Lightfish is about 11 feet long and 340 pounds, solar powered, and rated for multi-month endurance on station. Two people can launch and recover one from a boat ramp or a pickup truck. The company says its swappable sensor bay has carried infrared and daylight cameras, radio-signal payloads and sonar on earlier missions, so one hull can be set up for different sensing jobs.

Assistant Secretary of War for Homeland Defense and Americas Security Affairs Mark R. Ditlevson said the Lightfish has been prototyped and piloted on the Rio Grande and in the Gulf, calling it part of efforts to "gain 100% operational control of our borders."

fields.headline: XTEND TO BUILD 6,000 STRIKER DRONES
fields.deck: The $40.5 million order follows a top Gauntlet II finish in close quarters combat.

stories.caption:
XTEND AI Robotics, Inc. (NYSE: XTND) has received a $40.5 million order for 6,000 STRIKER systems. The order comes after XTEND was named a top performer in the Close Quarters Battle segment of Gauntlet II, the second gauntlet in the U.S. Department of War's Drone Dominance Program, a $1 billion iterative effort. CEO Aviv Shapira said the order reflects trust in the company's technology and its ability to deliver at scale.

STRIKER runs on XTEND's proprietary XOS operating system and is built for tactical work in confined, complex and GNSS-denied settings, where satellite navigation signals may be unreliable. The company says the order also reflects how STRIKER performed in a government-run evaluation against a competitive field.

Under the program's structure, Gauntlet II awardees move straight to Gauntlet III in the mission set where they were selected, but only after fulfilling a 400-system production order. Phase 3 of the program opened September 28, 2026. Gauntlet III performance will determine whether any Phase 3 orders are placed, and taking part does not guarantee an award.

Source: XTEND, 13OCT26

fields.headline: ARMY TO TEST COUNTER-DRONE TECH IN AFRICA
fields.deck: The partnership aims to deliver tested systems to Soldiers within 180 days.

stories.caption:
The U.S. Army Southern European Task Force, Africa (SETAF-AF) has teamed with the Army's Global Tactical Edge Acquisition Directorate (G-TEAD) to put emerging systems through testing in Africa, with the goal of getting proven ones into Soldiers' hands within 180 days.

The first accelerated capability event (ACE) is set for spring 2027 in Tan-Tan, Morocco. It will center on counter-unmanned aircraft systems and force protection, aimed at shielding early-entry command posts and operating locations from Group 1–3 small UAS. The Army points to Africa's open spectrum, uncongested airspace and varied terrain as conditions that let Soldiers validate solutions in theater before scaling them across the service.

Each ACE runs in three phases: submission and preparation, Soldier-led demonstrations and follow-on operational evaluation. SETAF-AF plans a Soldier-led demonstration in February and March 2027. The operational assessment comes next, in April and May, during the 2027 iteration of African Lion. G-TEAD will validate up to 15 solutions with PAE Fires as the transition partner.

Source: U.S. Army, October 16, 2026

fields.headline: ANTHEIA GETS CONDITIONAL $80M LOAN OFFER
fields.deck: The Office of Strategic Capital would fund onshoring of critical drug ingredients.

stories.caption:
Antheia, a biosynthesis company based in Menlo Park, Calif., has received a conditional commitment from the Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital for a direct, long-term loan of up to $80 million. The company says the financing, alongside additional private capital, would support its U.S. manufacturing strategy to onshore critical pharmaceutical ingredients.

The U.S. relies on foreign countries for about 90 percent of its supply of key starting materials and active pharmaceutical ingredients, a dependence the department's release links to drug shortages from public health emergencies, natural disasters, geopolitical tensions and supply chain failures. Antheia says it has previously received $32 million in non-dilutive federal financing and equity from strategic government-affiliated investors.

The commitment is conditional. Antheia must complete further financial, legal, technical, investment and due diligence requirements before financial close.

Source: Department of War, Oct. 18, 2026
